t: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Army” for construction of the Safeguard anti-ballistic missile system as authorized by section 401(a)(1), Public Law 92–156, $98,500,000, to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation of funds for military construction. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Army” for construction of the Safeguard anti-ballistic missile system

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing the expenditure of funds for a specific military construction project. It does not mention any consultation, coordination, public comment, advisory boards, or other forms of participation with entities outside the federal government. The reference to Public Law 92-156 is merely a citation of prior authorization, not a requirement for current participation.
qwen_block.s: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Army” for construction of the Safeguard anti-ballistic missile system as authorized by section 401(a)(1), Public Law 92–156, $98,500,000, to remain available until expended.

opus.w: This is a plain appropriation that provides funds for Army construction of the Safeguard missile system. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The reference to an earlier authorizing law is just a citation, not a process for outsiders to take part.
opus.s: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Army” for construction of the Safeguard anti-ballistic missile system as authorized by section 401(a)(1), Public Law 92–156, $98,500,000, to remain available until expended.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** One could misread the phrase "as authorized by section 401(a)(1), Public Law 92–156" as a procedural step. It isn't. It only points to the law that authorized the construction. This section is a plain appropriation for Army military construction. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, asked to comment, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause that authorizes the spending of funds for a specific construction project. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation with outside parties, public hearings, advisory committees with non-federal members, or any other form of participation as defined. The reference to Public Law 92-156 is merely to cite the legal authority for the project, not to invoke a participation process within this text.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount for “Military Construction, Army” for construction of the Safeguard anti-ballistic missile system as authorized by section 401(a)(1), Public Law 92–156, $98,500,000, to remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the construction is "authorized by section 401(a)(1), Public Law 92–156," and that other law might contain participation requirements, this section implicitly involves participation. However, the definition requires the *section itself* to recommend or require participation. This section is purely an appropriation clause. It allocates funds. It does not mention any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory board with outside members, or right to sue. It does not even mention who will build it or how the decision to build it was made, other than referencing prior authorization. Therefore, it fails the definition.
